content.title: Indiana’s Severe Weather Preparedness Week continues: Breaking down the difference between a watch and...
content.text: FORT WAYNE, Ind. (21Alive) - This week is Indiana’s Severe Weather Preparedness Week and one of the big marks of it includes the statewide tornado drill test that happened Tuesday morning.During this week, the National Weather Service goes over topics like response, recovery, and warnings which happens to be Tuesday’s topic.Warnings and watches are different, and certain protocols should be followed with both.A watch indicates there is a chance severe weather can happen. It does not mean it will take place but means get ready! One thing you can do is find a way to receive weather information. Some good tools include having a NOAA Weather Radio handy, Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA), and downloading the First Alert Weather App.A warning means that severe weather is happening or about to happen. When one is issued that means you should act immediately and head to your safest spot in your house. Usually, this is the basement or the lowest level of your home.Watch vs. Warning(WPTA)Let’s explain the difference using a cupcake.A watch indicates ingredients are in place for a cupcake to be made. Flour, sugar, baking soda are just a few necessary things to make one, so this means to be prepared!A warning indicates the cupcakes are ready, so act quickly. You should either eat them soon or someone else may and they’ll be gone!Cupcake Watch vs. Cupcake Warning(WPTA)Copyright 2024 WPTA. All rights reserved.
